feedback:
The revision closes most of the previous round's defects, and I verified each against the current text before judging the new review. D-036 records direct Developer ID distribution as a decision with the specification's own basis, so no self-declared blocking question stands against an architecture that assumes its answer. D-009 replaces length-based rejection with a settability probe, an approved pre-effect error class that ships empty, version-scoped expiring profiles and a content-based confirmation predicate, and it excludes messaging failures from the class permanently. D-010 supplies a complete attempt-state set with rejection demoted to a rung outcome and the rung handoff in one transaction. D-037 gives notes a run of their own with derived segments, content-addressed assignment revisions and dependency rows, and D-029 adds result_dependencies so a non-result input can be named. D-003 gives diarization its own sandboxed service and D-028 removes the external-decoder trust transfer. D-038 and D-040 separate retained identity from retained weights and register the materialized copies. D-041 keeps identity computable from bytes so an unlabeled local import activates. D-042 puts a working-data contract on every job and measures every process. D-014, D-016, D-011, D-006, D-033 and D-007 each resolve their prior objection. Those objections no longer apply.

Of the new review's ten blocking items, seven hold against the current text and three are overstated.

Holding. (1) Windowed diarization has contradictory persistence semantics. D-023 and D-042 both say windowed operation commits segment rows per window, while D-007 and the recovery table in the data lifecycle both say no partial diarization and no window results are committed on cancellation or interruption. Nothing reconciles them, so the durability of window output, its visibility, its cleanup after cancel or delete, and the transaction that publishes a complete diarization result are all undetermined; this is persistent-data behavior the specification forbids deferring. (2) D-037 carries assigned_by_user forward into a new diarization wherever derived segments overlap in time. Time overlap after a boundary change does not establish that the user assigned that speaker on those boundaries, so an inferred mapping inherits the evidentiary status the rest of D-023 is careful to withhold; the carried state should be unverified until confirmed. (3) The production path for meeting alignment is undefined. D-023 claims tone-derived drift correction and the Meetings coverage repeats it, but the only tones in the design are injected during the verification fixture, and a rate measured on fixture hardware does not transfer to an arbitrary user device. Either host-time alignment is the production mechanism with a stated behavior when residual drift exceeds the range, or the design must say where a real meeting gets its reference. (4) Admission priority is defined for one slot. D-004 reserves speech-primary for an interactive run and preempts batch speech, and says nothing about the generation slot, so an interactive rewrite can wait behind a batch meeting-notes job, which is the exact failure D-004's rationale names. Cross-slot conflict against the summed 8 GB budget is likewise unstated. The cancelled-seal path adds a second, smaller gap: sealing continues on the admission-exempt capture lane after cancellation returns, and the one-live-session rule does not bound how many such finalizers accumulate. (5) D-008 revalidates before each event-based rung and before Return, which excludes rung 1. Focus can move between the probe and the AXSelectedText write, and the ladder then writes into an element the focus-change policy says should be held or redirected, so policy and mechanism disagree for the preferred rung. (6) The D-030 data record carries per-packet byte sizes but no valid-frame, priming-frame or remainder-frame information, and CAF requires those to express the exact valid duration; the source chunks may already be deleted when recovery needs them, and F3 asserts packet count and decodability rather than decoded frame count and trimming. The consequence is bounded, at most a partial final packet, but the claim that the index carries everything needed to reconstruct the table is not yet true. (7) Materialized caches have conflicting ownership. The path is keyed by setHash while the registry and the deletion triggers are keyed by installation, and D-022 with D-041 deliberately allows two installations to share one content hash under different notices, so archiving one can remove the copy the other is using. Adapter removal is stated four ways: D-040 lists it as a deletion trigger, while D-038, the evolution section and the verification case all require the copy to survive as orphaned_runtime.

Also holding, in verification. The mode rubric pass rule is non-monotone: it forbids a zero on three criteria and caps the share of ones on any criterion, so every item can score zero on vocabulary terms intact or on formatting and the revision still ships. The translation rule has the same shape for no added content. Separately, recognition has no absolute acceptance basis anywhere; F1 compares the shipping adapter against a whisper.cpp harness at a relative margin, so two unusable transcribers satisfy the criterion, and no other protocol scores recognition on its own terms.

Overstated. The demand in item 1 that automatic delivery stop wherever a known counterexample can pass the checks is not satisfiable by any design, and REVIEW_NOTES says so directly: it asks for a defined consequence of an observed violation and an explicit scope per check, not a runtime proof for every utterance. D-012 now supplies both, gives the unsupported-sentence case a stated consequence, fails the automatic path closed for an unpacked language and for prose context, distils every source by default, and the Built-in modes and Context coverage entries state the residual limit rather than claiming enforcement. Item 9 is mostly answered: the automated long-input check already asserts a per-duration ceiling and a flat fitted slope in each participating process including DecodeService and a decoder child, so what is missing is a numbered range and failure action in the protocol list rather than a criterion. In item 8, publishing an unmet latency figure rather than concealing it matches the specification's honesty clause, though routing that outcome back to the named approver would be consistent with D-035; and ranges recorded as proposed with their basis, to be approved by the owner before each gate runs, are a legitimate design output rather than an unresolved decision that blocks deriving phases.

Item 10 sits between the two groups and I count it as holding in a narrow form. D-025 is much improved: manual by default, no automatic media key, ownership revoked by an observed transition, a stream gap or a mismatched state read. What is missing is the completeness property of the stream itself. The assumption entry verifies only that a state-change source exists, not that it is ordered and gap-detectable, so an adapter classified observing on an unverified notification source can miss a play, read paused at resume time, and reverse a manual pause. The observing conformance level should require an ordered gap-detectable stream or a second token such as playback position that proves no intervening change, and any adapter lacking it stays controlling-only.

One smaller conflict is worth folding into the same pass: the failure behavior says a failed user import stays in staging with its error attached, while the recovery sweep removes staged model directories without qualification.

Not stuck. Every confirmed defect is resolvable inside the design as written and needs no evidence the material cannot supply: choose durable or job-local for window output and give it visibility, cleanup and a publish transaction; mark carried assignments unverified; name the production alignment mechanism and its out-of-range behavior; state priority and preemption for every slot, for cross-slot budget conflict, and a concurrency bound for background finalization; revalidate before every external write; add the frame-count fields and assert decoded duration in F3; decide whether a materialized cache belongs to a content hash or an installation and make adapter removal consistent across the four places that describe it; make both pass rules monotone across scores and add a recognition acceptance basis that does not depend only on the comparator.

Check mapping. requirements is false for the Meetings contradictions and alignment gap, the carry-forward evidence status, the Text delivery revalidation gap for the preferred rung, and the Desktop behavior ownership-completeness gap. architecture is false for priority defined on one slot only, unbounded post-cancellation finalization on the exempt capture lane, and the materialized-cache ownership conflict across D-038, D-040 and the evolution section. alternatives is true: each decision, including the new D-036 through D-042, weighs options that were genuinely available with costs stated. data_lifecycle is false for the window-commit contradiction, the missing frame-count fields, the setHash-versus-installation keying, and the staged-import lifetime conflict. failures is false because the diarizing cancellation and recovery rows contradict the windowed design they are meant to cover, and because the delivery ladder omits revalidation before rung 1. maintainability is true: the ordering, gates, extension paths, runtime-replacement bound and accepted costs are specific and follow from the decisions, and the single conflicting sentence about adapter removal is scored under data_lifecycle and architecture rather than counted again here. verification is false for the two non-monotone pass rules, the absent absolute recognition basis, the F3 assertion that checks packets rather than decoded frames, and the absent range and action for decoder memory. unresolved_decisions is false because window persistence, cross-slot priority, materialized-cache ownership on a shared hash, revalidation before the accessibility write, and the production drift correction are all left to whichever implementation task reaches them first.
